title: Design the change
goal: The change has a plan that can be worked: how it connects to the other work in flight, what is said to whom and when, the roles afterwards, the measures of adoption, and the hours and money it needs, all approved by the founder.

steps.do: Name every other piece of work in flight that touches the same process, tool or person, and say for each whether it must land first, can land together or must wait.
Write the change as an ordered set of handoffs with done criteria, the smallest first, each one reversible on its own, and say what is left in place until the handoff after it passes.
Write what each affected person must be able to do afterwards and how they will be walked through it, using the new process record's steps as the material.

consider.why: A new way of working that nobody has been shown is run as the old way with new names.
consider.when: Someone other than the person designing the change will run the new steps.

steps.do: Draft what is said to each affected group, when it is said and by whom, mark every message that goes outside the venture, and leave each of those for the founder to send.
Bring the founder the name proposed to carry the change with what it would ask of them, and record the assignment once the founder has asked them and they have agreed.

consider.why: Asking a person to carry a change is a commitment only the founder makes.
consider.when: The plan depends on someone other than the founder changing how they work.

steps.do: Set out the ways the new way of working could be made worth doing, time given back, a task removed, or payment, with what each costs, and leave the choice and any money to the founder.

consider.why: A change that makes someone's day worse is undone quietly, so what they get for it is worth naming.
consider.when: The change adds work for a person who is paid by the venture.

steps.do: Name how it will be known that the new way is actually being used, the share of runs that followed the new steps and the share that fell back, and say where each is read and how often.
Write who does what after the change, process record by process record, with one owner each, and name any step that would end up with nobody doing it.
Total the hours and the money the plan needs, by handoff, name the role each hour falls on, and bring the total to the founder as the ask before any of it is spent.
Raise the plan to the founder for a yes or no as a whole, with the order of the handoffs and the point at which it could still be stopped.

done_criteria.check: Is the change broken into handoffs that can be undone one at a time, and does every step after the change have exactly one owner?
